decisions.reason: Metro data centre connectivity runs on owned fibre, has shown early adoption by data centres and financial hubs, and fits the high-bandwidth strategy, so it stays at low carrying cost even though recent website evidence is missing.
Optical spectrum services use the owned fibre at little extra cost and serve growing hyperscale and carrier bandwidth demand, so the option is still worth more open than closed.
The self-service number ordering portal costs little to run and supports the voice business and the real-time provisioning direction, though it may later be folded into a broader platform.
Direct SIP-type voice connectivity remains core to enterprise voice and cloud telephony migration, is cheap to maintain on the owned network, and has not shown results that justify abandoning it.
